beats.text: Your heart is racing. Your hands are shaking. Everyone can tell. Right?
Psychologists call it the illusion of transparency. We think our feelings are written all over our face.
In studies on public speaking, speakers thought they looked far more nervous than the audience saw them.
Speakers who learned about this illusion before their talk felt calmer. And the audience rated their speeches better.
And now you know about it too.

sources: Gilovich, Savitsky & Medvec (1998). The illusion of transparency. JPSP 75(2).

Savitsky & Gilovich (2003). The illusion of transparency and the alleviation of speech anxiety. JESP 39. Speakers overestimated how visible their nervousness was; those informed about the illusion felt less anxious and observers rated their speeches better.
